## Brand Strategy
This is a typography addendum to broader Ogilvy Brand Guidelines, not a standalone document. It positions Ogilvy as "founded on words" and "naturally a heavily typographic brand," establishing typographic voice as central to brand identity. The document is deeply educational, providing historical context and craft-level typographic instruction.

## Logo
Not covered in this addendum (covered in main brand guidelines). One note: the Ogilvy logo is derived from the Ogilvy Serif letterforms. A "gi" ligature exists in the logo but is deliberately excluded from the fonts to prevent accidental logo recreation.

## Typography
This is the core of the document. Extremely detailed coverage:

### Typeface Families
1. **Ogilvy Sans** -- Grotesque sans-serif with heritage from Johnston (London Underground). Geometric capitals, American-style grotesque lowercase. Three weights: Light, Regular, Bold (each with italic companion). Italic is technically a sloped roman (17-degree slope). Alternate characters for a, t, y.
2. **Ogilvy Serif** -- Transitional serif inspired by Baskerville (the original Ogilvy brand typeface). True italic (22-degree slope) with distinct letterforms. Three weights: Light, Regular, Bold (each with italic companion). Extensive ligature set (standard and discretionary). Three numeral sets: Proportional Oldstyle (preferred), Proportional Lining (default), Tabular Lining (tables only).

### Design Relationship
The two families share proportional, structural, and stylistic similarities -- designed as a matching set. They occupy roughly the same horizontal space and are interchangeable without harming layout. X-height is exactly 2/3 cap height in both.

### Key Structural Differences
- Serif: wide capitals, fluid forms, high stroke contrast, flamboyant Q, ligatures, teardrop terminal on ampersand
- Sans: narrow capitals, geometric forms, low stroke contrast, calm Q, no ligatures, one-storey alternates

### Headline Settings
- **Sans Light:** Leading = type size, tracking -10, word spacing 90%, optical kerning
- **Sans Regular:** Leading = type size, tracking -15, word spacing 85%, optical kerning
- **Serif Light:** Leading = type size, tracking -15, word spacing 65%, optical kerning
- **Serif Regular:** Leading = type size, tracking -10, word spacing 75%, optical kerning

### Body Copy Rules
- Default leading: 20% (standard). 10pt = 12pt leading, 20pt = 24pt leading
- Wordspacing: Minimum 65%, Desired 85%, Maximum 100%
- Always ragged left (no force justification, no center or right justify for body)
- Measure: 50-75 characters per line (ideal: 66 characters)
- Margins: Goldilocks approach -- not too much, not too little

### Grids
- Always even-numbered columns: 2, 4 (basic), 6, 12 (advanced)
- Not all columns need to be used

### Ampersands
Six variations across the two families. Alternate serif ampersands (with teardrop terminal variations) are preferred when possible.

### Font Substitution
- Ogilvy Sans substitutes with **Arial** (nearly identical space)
- Ogilvy Serif substitutes with **Times New Roman** (similar proportions, less space)
- Substitutes only for internal use; never for external marketing, press, or print

### Numeral Systems
- Sans: Proportional Lining (preferred) + Tabular Lining
- Serif: Proportional Oldstyle (preferred) + Proportional Lining + Tabular Lining
- Tabular Lining numeral "1" has two variants (with/without wide foot)

## Applications
Typography application guidance is embedded throughout: signage, headlines, stationery, digital applications, mobile apps, documents, publications, presentations, PowerPoint/Keynote files, PDFs.

## Tone of Voice
Not directly covered, but the document's own writing voice is notably sophisticated, historically informed, and confident. It reflects Ogilvy's positioning as an authority on communication craft. References to typographic history (Francesco Griffo, Aldus Manutius, Robert Estienne, Simon de Colines, John Baskerville) demonstrate intellectual depth.

## Outliers / Unique Elements
- This is one of the most detailed typography-only brand documents in the collection. Its depth is exceptional -- covering italic history, numeral classification, ligature behavior, wordspacing mathematics, and structural analysis of individual letterforms.
- The explicit comparison pages showing structural differences between Sans and Serif (character by character) are unusually thorough.
- The "gi ligature" prohibition (to prevent accidental logo creation) is a clever brand protection detail.
- The document functions simultaneously as brand guidelines and a typography education resource.
- Custom typefaces by COLLINS and MCKL with licensing restrictions (not freely distributable).
- The Johnston (London Underground) heritage connection for Ogilvy Sans is an interesting design lineage choice.
- Wordspacing rules are specified with mathematical precision (Minimum/Desired/Maximum percentages).

## Quality Score
**5/5** -- An exceptional typography addendum that sets a very high standard for typographic brand documentation. The depth of coverage is remarkable: from historical context to precise setting specifications, from structural letterform analysis to practical font substitution guidance. Every aspect of typographic implementation is addressed with clarity and authority. The educational approach (explaining why, not just what) makes it both a brand tool and a reference document. The only limitation is its narrow scope (typography only), but within that scope it is among the best examples available.
